# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed brought about the child's conception. I defend the standard reading: Jesus Christ was conceived in Mary without any man, by the Holy Ghost. Joseph was his supposed father and legal guardian, not his begetter.

## 1. Mary was a virgin who had not come together with any man

- [L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] The Greek behind "came together" is *sunerchomai* (G4905, to come together, here the union of husband and wife). The conception is placed before that union. The Greek behind "virgin" is *parthenos* (G3933, a maiden who has not known a man).
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *Ginosko* (G1097, to know) is used here for sexual knowledge. *Aner* (G435, a man, a male person) shows that Mary points to the absence of any male.
- [L3] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." The Hebrew is *almah* (H5959), which the KJV renders "virgin". Matthew 1:23 quotes it: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."
- [L4] Mary says she knows no man, and the text places her pregnancy before any coming together with Joseph. Her pregnancy therefore has no male source.

## 2. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost

- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] The preposition is *ek* (G1537, out of, from, denoting origin or source). The participle is *gennao* (G1080, to beget or conceive), in the passive. The thing begotten in her has its origin *out of* the Holy Ghost.
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *Episkiazo* (G1982, to overshadow) is the word for the working of divine power. *Dia touto* ("therefore", G1223 with G3778) makes the title follow from the manner of conception.
- [L4] Luke 1:34 asks how this can be without a man. Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and names no man. The source of the child is stated and it is not a man.

## 3. Joseph's place is legal and supposed, not generative

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] *Enomizeto* (G3543, was supposed, was reckoned by custom or opinion) marks "son of Joseph" as the common opinion and not the fact.
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L2] The chain of "begat" ends at Joseph. The birth is "of whom" (*ex hes*, G1537 with a feminine singular relative), which refers to Mary alone and not to Joseph.
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *Ginosko* (G1097, to know) is again the idiom of marital union. It is negated up to the birth.
- [L4] Joseph is minded to put away a wife found with child, and the angel must tell him to take her. He is told the source (Matthew 1:20) and does not know it by himself. Matthew 1:25 says he had no union with her until the birth. Joseph therefore stands as husband and guardian, not as begetter.

## 4. The pattern of Scripture agrees

- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his son, made of a woman, made under the law."
- [L2] *Ginomai* (G1096, to become, to be made) is used of the child, with the woman named as the one he came of. No man is named in the generation.
- [L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed." The Hebrew *zera* (H2233, seed) is credited to the woman.
- [L3] Jeremiah 31:22: "the LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man." The Hebrew *bara* (H1254, to create) marks the thing as a new work of the LORD and not an ordinary generation.
- [L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
- [L1] Luke 2:48: "Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?"
- [L4] When Mary says "thy father" of Joseph, the child answers by pointing to "my father's business" (Luke 2:49), which is not Joseph's. The child corrects the phrase used for Joseph.

## 5. Anticipated objections

- [L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" The speakers are the crowd, "they said". [L3] Luke 3:23, "as was supposed", shows that this was common opinion.
- [L1] Luke 2:48 "thy father" is a form of address within the household. [L3] The reply at Luke 2:49 names another father.
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." [L2] *Sperma* (G4690, seed) is here descent, a line. [L3] Matthew 1:16 has the birth "of whom", Mary. [L3] Luke 1:32 gives the throne of "his father David", which is the line of descent and not a claim of a begetting by Joseph.

DECLARED CHAIN

1. Mary was a virgin, had not come together with Joseph, and knew no man: [L1] Luke 1:27, Matthew 1:18, Luke 1:34; [L2] *sunerchomai* (to come together), *ginosko* (to know); [L3] Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23, *almah* (virgin).
2. The conception is stated to be of the Holy Ghost: [L1] Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek* (out of, source) and *episkiazo* (to overshadow); [L3] Luke 1:34 asks how without a man, and Luke 1:35 answers with divine power.
3. Joseph is the supposed father and husband, not the begetter: [L1] Luke 3:23, Matthew 1:16, Matthew 1:25; [L2] *enomizeto* (was supposed), *ex hes* (feminine "of whom"); [L3] Matthew 1:19-20 on Joseph's decision to put her away and the angel's explanation.
4. The wider Scripture pattern puts the woman and the new creation at the source: [L1] Galatians 4:4; [L2] *ginomai* (to be made), *bara* (to create); [L3] Genesis 3:15, Jeremiah 31:22, Hebrews 10:5, Luke 2:48-49.
5. Christ had no biological father: no man's seed was the source of his conception; the Holy Ghost is stated as the source, and the child was born of Mary.

# Round 2: the defender answers

I answer the challenger's presses in order, beginning with the question put to me. Where a press lands, I say so.

## The question: how is it evident (Hebrews 7:14) that our Lord sprang out of Juda?

- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L2] *prodēlos* (G4271, plain before all men) is the word for "evident". *anatetalken* (G393 *anatellō*, to arise, spring up) is the verb for "sprang". It is the verb of a rising, and it is not *gennaō* (G1080, to beget).
- [L1] Luke 2:4-5: Joseph went up to Bethlehem "because he was of the house and lineage of David", "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife".
- [L3] Matthew 1:20-21 and 1:24-25: Joseph is told "take unto thee Mary thy wife", he "took unto him his wife", and "he called his name JESUS".
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L4] The evidence is the public register. The law enrolled by the house of the father (Numbers 1:18). Joseph, of David's house (Luke 2:4), took the mother and named the child (Matthew 1:24-25). The child was therefore enrolled in Joseph's house, and "supposed" (Luke 3:23) is the word for that reckoning. The register records the house and does not report who begat. This route is evident to all (G4271) and requires no seed from Joseph.
- [L3] Ezra 2:61 shows a man "called after their name" by a house he entered through a wife, which is a naming by house and not a begetting. Ezra 2:62 names the failure: "they were not found". The failure is a register not found (*matsa'*, H4672, to find), not a rule excluding a wife's line.
- [L3] Luke 1:42, to Mary: "blessed is the fruit of thy womb." The word *karpos* (G2590, fruit) is the word of Acts 2:30, "the fruit of his loins". The promise-word "fruit" is used of Mary's womb in Luke's own text.
- [L1] Hebrews 7:16: "Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life." The same chapter that says "evident" sets the priesthood apart from a carnal rule of descent.

## Link D5: Romans 1:3, Acts 2:30, 2 Samuel 7:12, Hebrews 7:10

- [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." [L2] The verb is *ginomai* (G1096, to become, be made). The noun is *sperma* (G4690, something sown, "seed (including the male sperm); by implication, offspring"). *Sarx* (G4561, flesh) carries "the means of kindred".
- [L3] Romans 9:5: "of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came" is said of Israel as a people. [L4] "According to the flesh" in these rows marks kinship by descent, and it does not prove which parent carries it.
- [L3] Genesis 3:15 gives "her seed" to the woman (H2233, seed, posterity). Galatians 3:29: "then are ye Abraham's seed". [L4] "Seed" is used where no loins are in view, so the word alone does not set a man's act as the source.
- [L1] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." The "father" is Abraham, the forefather of Levi, as the verse's own context shows (Hebrews 7:5, "the loins of Abraham"). [L3] *patēr* (G3962) means a remote forefather in Matthew 3:9, "We have Abraham to our father", and Luke 1:73, "our father Abraham". [L4] Loins in Hebrews 7:10 are an ancestor's across generations. They are not a claim that the last man in a line begat. The press makes loins an immediate father's act, and the verse does not use them that way.
- I withdraw the term "legal guardian" as an office word. What the rows give is this: Joseph took his wife (Matthew 1:24), named the child (Matthew 1:25), and the child "was subject unto them" (Luke 2:51). I keep "supposed father" ([L1] Luke 3:23).
- Luke 1:32, "his father David": [L3] the forefather sense of *patēr* above means the phrase names David as ancestor. I do not rest it on Mary's house.

## Link D3

**Luke 3:23.** [L2] *enomizeto* (G3543, was reckoned, deemed by custom) is the same form as Acts 16:13, "was wont". I grant that it states what was customary. [L4] Luke writes it in his own narrator's voice inside a genealogy and attaches it to "son of Joseph". That is a reckoning marked as a reckoning, and the same Luke gave the source at Luke 1:35.

**The voices.** [L1] Luke 2:48 (Mary), [L3] Luke 4:22 and John 1:45 (the town, Philip), and John 6:42 (the crowd) are speakers' reckonings. [L3] John 6:42 sits beside the same crowd's "whose father and mother we know", the very supposition Luke 3:23 marks. Luke's own narration names the two of them differently. [L3] Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled". [L3] Luke 2:43: "Joseph and his mother knew not of it." [L3] The angel's phrase is "the young child and his mother" (Matthew 2:13). [L4] The narrator and the angel never say "his father and mother" in these verses. The speakers do. The "parents" of Luke 2:27 and 2:41 name the household that carried him.

**Matthew 1:16 against Genesis 4:25.** I grant Eve's "another seed" sits beside "Adam knew his wife". [L1] Matthew 1:25 puts the opposite beside the mother: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". [L3] Matthew 1:2-16 repeats "begat" at every link, and at the last the verb changes to "of whom was born Jesus" (the feminine *ex hēs*, G1537 with a feminine relative). [L4] The sentence shifts the verb at the one place where the husband is named "the husband of Mary".

**Matthew 1:19-20 at its means.** The press says the angel joins the child to David's house through "Joseph, thou son of David". [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [L2] *gar* (G1063, for) gives the ground of "fear not to take". The ground stated is the source, "of the Holy Ghost". It is not the child's being Joseph's. [L2] *gennēthen* (G1080, begotten, as the KJV margin has it) is the verb: the thing begotten in her is of the Holy Ghost. [L4] The address "son of David" and the command to take her fit the legal route above (Matthew 1:24-25), and the reason that Matthew gives for the command is the Holy Ghost.

**The naming.** [L3] Luke 1:13 and 1:62 give the naming to the father. [L1] Luke 1:31 gives it to Mary: "shalt call his name JESUS". [L3] Luke 1:60: "his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John". [L3] Genesis 4:25: Eve "called his name Seth". [L4] The naming is done by either parent, so it does not mark Joseph as the begetter. It marks him, in Matthew 1:21-25, as the man who received the child.

**The timing.** [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child". I grant the challenger's reading that this "coming together" is the taking of Matthew 1:24. [L1] Matthew 1:25 then sets "knew her not till she had brought forth". [L4] On the challenger's own order, before the taking there was no coming together (1:18), and from the taking to the birth there was no knowing (1:25). That covers the whole pregnancy, so Joseph's seed has no place in the order. The "wife" title (Matthew 1:20; Deuteronomy 22:24) is a betrothal title and gives no knowing.

## Link D2

**Luke 1:35 at the word.** I correct my earlier Greek. The word is *dio kai* (G1352, wherefore, with *kai*, also), not *dia touto*. [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L4] The ground sits in the same verse, in the clause just before the "therefore". The "also" adds this ground to the title already given in Luke 1:32. It does not remove the ground.

**The answer to the "how".** [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L4] The angel answers with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, acting on her person. [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 grounds the sonship in "I have chosen him", and Luke 1:35 grounds it in what comes "upon thee". The grounds differ, so the covenant-title parallel does not cover Luke 1:35.

**The verbs.** [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904, to come upon) and *episkiazō* (G1982, to overshadow) mean presence and power at Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34 and Acts 5:15. I grant that. [L4] In Luke 1:35 the angel answers the "how" of a conception with these verbs, and the product is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The power acts upon Mary and produces the child, which Acts 1:8 does not do.

**John 1:13, 1 John 5:1, John 3:6.** [L1] John 1:13 itself rules out three human sources: "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." [L3] John 3:4 shows a believer's "born of God" is a second birth, after a first from the womb. [L1] Matthew 1:20 names the first begetting: "that which is conceived in her". [L4] A believer's divine begetting follows a natural one. Christ's divine begetting is the conception itself. I grant that *ek* (G1537, out of) is the same preposition in both places.

## Link D1

**Luke 1:34 tense.** [L4] The "how" is Mary's response to Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". She is already espoused (Luke 1:27) and her marriage is expected, yet she asks "how". Her question treats the conception as one to come while she knows no man. The angel does not reply with "after the taking". He names the Holy Ghost. [L1] Matthew 1:18 confirms the order: found with child "before they came together".

**Isaiah 7:14.** The KJV renders *almah* (H5959) "virgin" at Isaiah 7:14 and, in the quotation, *parthenos* (G3933) "virgin" at Matthew 1:23. [L3] Genesis 24:43, "when the virgin cometh forth", uses the same Hebrew word of Rebekah, whom Genesis 24:16 calls "a virgin, neither had any man known her". [L4] The KJV's "maid" and "damsels" at Exodus 2:8 and Psalm 68:25 are also unmarried girls. The press against "virgin" from the KJV's own range does not displace the KJV's own word at Isaiah 7:14.

**Isaiah 8:3-4.** [L1] Isaiah 8:3 gives "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz". The Immanuel child of Isaiah 7:14 has a different name, and the prophetess is a different woman. [L4] The text names two children by two names. Matthew 1:22-23 applies the "virgin" of 7:14, and Matthew 1:18 places Mary "before they came together".

## Link D4

I narrow D4. It supports the chain and does not carry it alone.

- **Galatians 4:4.** I grant that "born of women" (Matthew 11:11) is said of John, who had a father (Luke 1:13). [L1] Galatians 4:4 reads "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman". [L2] *ginomai* (G1096) here is "be made", and the Son is "sent forth" before he is "made of a woman". [L3] John 1:14: "the Word was made flesh". D4 fits the exclusion and does not state it. D1 and D2 carry the exclusion.
- **Genesis 3:15.** I grant that Genesis 4:25 sets "another seed" beside the knowing. The "her seed" of Genesis 3:15 fits and is not an independent proof.
- **Jeremiah 31:22.** I withdraw it from the chain. Its context (Jeremiah 31:21, "O virgin of Israel") is the nation's return, and I do not rest a premise on it.
- **Hebrews 10:5.** [L2] *katērtisō* (G2675, to fit, prepare) is God's act on the body. [L3] Hebrews 2:17, "in all things... like unto [his] brethren", is limited by Hebrews 4:15, "yet without sin". I take it as support only.
- **Luke 2:48-49.** I narrow "corrects" to "contrasts". [L1] Mary says "thy father", and the child answers "my Father's business". [L1] Luke 2:50 notes "they understood not the saying which he spake unto them". [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 shows a covenant father beside a fleshly one, and I grant that this reading fits Luke 2:49. [L4] The reversal of the possessive shows whose Father the child claims. It does not alone exclude Joseph, and I do not claim that it does.

## Where the case stands

- Matthew 1:18, 1:20 and 1:25 with Luke 1:34-35 carry the exclusion (D1, D2). The press reading "know not a man" as a present state fails to explain why the angel answers with the Holy Ghost.
- D3 and Hebrews 7:14 run on the register route, from Numbers 1:18, Luke 2:4-5 and Matthew 1:24-25.
- The Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 presses fail on the word "seed" (G4690, offspring) and on "fruit" at Luke 1:42.
- I withdraw "legal guardian" as an office term and withdraw Jeremiah 31:22. D4 is narrowed to a supporting link.

# DEFENDER'S OPENING

I am the defender. I open and hold the standard reading of this topic: **Christ had no biological father.** The record states that the child was conceived "of the Holy Ghost" in Mary, a virgin who "knew not a man," before she and Joseph "came together," and that Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." My method is fixed by the burden rule: I build only on rows that affirm. I require no verse to state a denial, and I rest on no verse's silence.

**The topic in the record's own words.** The record's word for biological fatherhood is "begat": [L1] Matthew 1:2 — "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;" — [L2] γεννάω (gennaō, G1080, "beget, become the father of"). [L4] On [L1] Matthew 1:2 and [L2] gennaō, together with the father-subject pattern of Matthew 1:2-16 exhibited in LINK 4 below: to have a biological father, in this record's terms, is to be begotten of a man. The question is what the record states about the begetting of Jesus. Five links carry the answer.

## LINK 1 — the record states the source of the child: "of the Holy Ghost"

[L1] Matthew 1:18 — "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] The verse opens with γένεσις (genesis, G1078, "birth, generation") and οὕτως (houtōs, G3779, "thus, on this wise"): the record announces that it will state the manner of the birth, and the first fact it states is the source — ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (ek pneumatos hagiou, "of the Holy Ghost"; πνεῦμα, pneuma, "spirit, ghost"; ἅγιος, hagios, "holy"), with ἐκ (ek, G1537, "of, out of," the preposition of source). The child is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost."

[L1] Matthew 1:19 — "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." — the record states the mind Joseph had on this finding.

[L1] Matthew 1:20 — "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] The same preposition of source stands again — ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου ("is of the Holy Ghost") — and the child is named τὸ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθέν (to en autē gennēthen, "that which is conceived in her"), from γεννάω (gennaō, G1080, "beget, conceive"), the same verb the record renders "begat" throughout Matthew 1. The ground-marker γάρ (gar, G1063, "for, because") shows what the stated origin is doing in the record: it is the reason the angel gives why Joseph should "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

[L3] Luke 1:35 — "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." — the same source, named to Mary.

[L4] Inference, on [L1] Matthew 1:18 + [L1] Matthew 1:20 + [L2] ek ("of, out of," source) and gennaō ("beget, conceive") + [L3] Luke 1:35: the record states the origin of the child three times — in the narrator's voice (Matthew 1:18), in the angel of the Lord's word to Joseph (Matthew 1:20), and in the angel Gabriel's word to Mary (Luke 1:35) — and every statement names the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception.

## LINK 2 — the record states the state of the mother: a virgin who has not known a man

[L1] Luke 1:26-27 — "And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."

[L2] παρθένος (parthenos, G3933, "virgin") stands twice in Luke 1:27 — "a virgin espoused," "the virgin's name was Mary" — and ἐμνηστευμένην (emnēsteumenēn, from μνηστεύω, G3423, "espoused, betrothed") marks her state, the same state Matthew 1:18 states: "espoused to Joseph."

[L1] Luke 1:31 — "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." — [L2] συλλήμψῃ (sylēmpsē, from συλλαμβάνω, G4815, "conceive") ἐν γαστρὶ (en gastri, "in womb") — γαστήρ (gastēr, G1064, "womb"): the promised child is conceived in her own womb.

[L1] Luke 1:34 — "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] γινώσκω (ginōskō, G1097, "know") with ἄνδρα (andra, "a man"): her stated state when the manner is announced — she has not known a man. The record itself joins her state to the question of the manner: her word is "How shall this be," and the answer it gives is Luke 1:35 (LINK 5).

[L3] Genesis 4:1 — "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD." — [L2] יָדַע (yada, H3045, "know") stands in this verse: the record's own idiom for the conjugal act — "knew... and she conceived." Mary's "I know not a man" is that idiom: the act has not occurred.

[L1] Isaiah 7:14 — "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

[L1] Matthew 1:22-23 — "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

[L2] The word standing in Isaiah 7:14 is עַלְמָה (almah, H5959), which the record renders "a virgin" there; the record's own quotation of the verse in Matthew 1:23 carries παρθένος (parthenos, G3933, "virgin"), and the conceiving-word of Isaiah 7:14 is הָרָה (harah, H2030, "with child, conceiving"). The record states that this — the virgin with child — is what "was fulfilled," and itself interprets the child's name: Emmanuel, "God with us" (עִמָּנוּ אֵל, immanu el, "with us God").

[L4] Inference, on [L1] Luke 1:27 + [L1] Luke 1:34 + [L2] parthenos ("virgin") and ginōskō ("know") + [L3] Genesis 4:1 + [L1] Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:22-23: the record states, at every point it touches the matter, that the one who conceives and bears is a virgin, espoused but not knowing a man; and the prophecy the record says was fulfilled in this birth is "a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."

## LINK 3 — the record states the time: found "before they came together," not known "till she had brought forth"

[L1] Matthew 1:18 — "...before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." — [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, "before they came together"); συνέρχομαι (synerchomai, G4905, "come together"): the record dates the finding of the child before the coming together of the espoused pair.

[L3] 1 Corinthians 7:5 — "Defraud ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency." — the record's own conjugal use of "come together," of husband and wife.

[L1] Matthew 1:24 — "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:"

[L1] Matthew 1:25 — "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures affirms that Christ was conceived in the womb of the virgin Mary by the Holy Ghost without the agency of a human father, and therefore did not have a biological father.

### I. The Conception Occurred Before Joseph and Mary Came Together

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek temporal prepositional phrase translated "before they came together" contains πρίν (*prin*, G4250, "before, formerly") and συνελθεῖν (*synelthein*, aorist active infinitive of συνέρχομαι, *synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together, to come together in cohabitation or conjugal union").
[L3] Matthew 1:25 confirms the absence of sexual intercourse until after the delivery: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Here "knew" renders ἔγινωσκεν (*eginōsken*, imperfect active of γινώσκω, *ginōskō*, G1097, used of carnal knowledge, as in Genesis 4:1).
[L4] Because Mary was already found with child prior to any conjugal union (*synelthein*) with Joseph, and Joseph "knew her not" until after the birth, Joseph was not the physical or biological generator of the child.

---

### II. Mary's Explicit Testimony of Carnal Inexperience

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] The Greek present active indicative verb γινώσκω (*ginōskō*, G1097, "to know, understand, perceive, have carnal relations with") is paired with the negative particle οὐ (*ou*, G3756, absolute negation) and ἄνδρα (*andra*, accusative singular of ἀνήρ, *anēr*, G435, "a male person, a husband, a man").
[L3] Genesis 19:8 exhibits the exact semantic force of knowing a man as sexual relations: "Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man."
[L4] Mary’s question establishes that at the time of the annunciation, she had no sexual relations with any male human being; therefore, the conception foretold could not proceed from human biological paternity.

---

### III. The Agency of Conception is the Holy Ghost and Divine Power

[L1] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] The Greek verb ἐπισκιάσει (*episkiasei*, future active indicative of ἐπισκιάζω, *episkiazō*, G1982) means "to overshadow, to cast a shade upon, to envelop in divine presence."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek phrase translated "is conceived" is τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν (*to gar en autē gennēthen*, aorist passive participle of γεννάω, *gennaō*, G1080, "to beget, to bear, to bring forth"), modified by the prepositional phrase ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου (*ek pneumatos estin hagiou*, "is of the Holy Ghost").
[L4] The origin and conception of the holy child was wrought by the divine overshadowing of the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatos hagiou*), operating upon the womb of Mary, entirely replacing and excluding the biological seed or agency of a human male.

---

### IV. The Fulfillment of the Prophecy of the Virgin Birth

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] The Hebrew noun translated "virgin" is עַלְמָה (*‘almāh*, H5959, "a virgin, a young maiden of marriageable age who is unmarried and sexually untouched").
[L3] Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." In Matthew 1:23, the text employs the Greek noun ἡ παρθένος (*hē parthenos*, G3933, "the virgin"), an explicit technical designation for an unmarried woman who has preserved her chastity.
[L4] Prophecy required that the mother conceive while retaining the status of a virgin (*parthenos*); a conception occurring through the natural biological agency of a human male would extinguish that status and falsify the divine sign.

---

### V. Legal Paternity Versus Biological Origin in the Genealogies

[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli."
[L2] The Greek parenthetical participle phrase ὢν ὡς ἐνομίζετο (*ōn hōs enomizeto*) employs ἐνομίζετο (imperfect passive of νομίζω, *nomizō*, G3543, "to hold by custom, to deem, to reckon, to suppose according to custom or law").
[L3] Matthew 1:16 departs from the generational formula "A begat B" used in the preceding fifteen verses: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." In Matthew 1:16, the relative pronoun "of whom" is feminine singular in the Greek: ἐξ ἧς (*ex hēs*), referring exclusively to Mary, whereas every prior generation in the genealogy from verses 2 to 16 uses the active verb ἐγέννησεν (*egennēsen*, "begat") applied to the male ancestor.
[L4] While Joseph was the customary and legal father according to the civic registers (*hōs enomizeto*), the scripture deliberately breaks the male begetting formula (*egennēsen*) at Joseph, attributing the birth exclusively to Mary (*ex hēs*), confirming that Joseph was not Christ's biological progenitor.

---

### DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew 1:18 exhibits that Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost before coming together (G4905, *synelthein*) with Joseph, and Matthew 1:25 exhibits that Joseph knew her not (G1097, *ginōskō*) till she brought forth her firstborn son.
2. Luke 1:34 exhibits that Mary had no carnal knowledge of a man (G1097, *ginōskō*), supported by Genesis 19:8 establishing that knowing a man signifies sexual relations.
3. Luke 1:35 and Matthew 1:20 exhibit that the conception was directly effected by the overshadowing (G1982, *episkiazō*) of the Holy Ghost, and generated of the Holy Ghost (G1080, *gennaō*).
4. Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23 exhibit that Christ was conceived by an untouched virgin (H5959, *‘almāh*; G3933, *parthenos*) without the natural biological seed of a man.
5. Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16 exhibit that Joseph was the father only by custom and legal reckoning (G3543, *nomizō*), with the genealogy attributing physical birth solely to the mother (feminine relative pronoun *ex hēs*).
6. Christ did not have a biological father.

**Position.** The KJV says Jesus was conceived of Mary, a virgin, by the Holy Ghost. Joseph is his husband-guardian and legal father: he takes Mary, names the child, and carries David's house. The text does not make him the begetter. I answer the declared chain D1-D5 point by point and then set out the case.

---

## A. The conception came before Joseph and Mary came together, and its source is the Holy Ghost

**A1.** [L1] "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:18
[L2] sunerchomai (G4905) means to come together, and in the marriage setting to live together as husband and wife. ek (G1537) means out of, from, source; the source of the child is "the Holy Ghost".
[L3] "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child." Luke 2:5
[L4] Mary is found with child before the coming together (Matthew 1:18). She is still "espoused" while "great with child" (Luke 2:5), so the coming together had not yet happened at the late stage of her pregnancy. The defender's D4 says the begetting falls "within the espousal before the withheld span". Matthew 1:18 puts the child before the coming together, and the only source it names is the Holy Ghost. D4's order is therefore reversed.

**A2.** [L1] "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Matthew 1:25
[L2] heos hou (G2193 with the relative) means up to which time. ginosko (G1097) means to know.
[L3] "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" Matthew 1:24
[L4] The angel speaks of the child as already "conceived in her" (Matthew 1:20) before Joseph takes her (Matthew 1:24). The not-knowing of Matthew 1:25 then runs "till she had brought forth", which covers the whole span of the pregnancy. The conception sits before both the taking and the not-knowing. D4 reads Matthew 1:24-25 as putting the begetting "before the withheld span" and giving it to Joseph. But Matthew 1:20 and Matthew 1:18 give that conception to the Holy Ghost.

---

## B. The angel's reason to Joseph names the Holy Ghost, not Joseph

**B1.** [L1] "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20
[L2] gar (G1063) means for, giving the reason. gennao (G1080), in the passive gennethen, means begotten, as the margin notes. The begotten thing is "in her" and is "of" (ek) the Holy Ghost.
[L3] "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:19
[L4] Joseph intends to put her away (Matthew 1:19). The angel's stated reason to take her anyway is "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). The meaning of that reason is that the begotten child has its origin from the Holy Ghost, which is why Joseph's resolve to put her away is lifted. A reason that named Joseph as the begetter would not remove his cause for concern. This answers the defender's reading of Matthew 1:19-20 as a husband begetting his wife's child.

**B2.** The defender's gloss on gennao says "by extension of the mother", and Matthew 1:20 places what is begotten "in her". The origin ek is the Holy Ghost.
[L1] "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:21
[L3] "Thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." Luke 1:13
[L4] Zacharias is told the son is borne "thee", for him. Joseph is told "she shall bring forth a son" and "thou shalt call his name". Joseph's role is the naming.

---

## C. Mary's question and the angel's answer

**C1.** [L1] "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:34
[L2] ginosko (G1097) means to know, the same word the defender cites for Matthew 1:25. andra (G435) means a man, a male, a husband.
[L3] "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary." Luke 1:27
[L4] Mary is espoused to Joseph (Luke 1:27) yet says "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34), using the defender's own word "know". D4 says the canon's stated means of begetting is knowing (Genesis 4:1, Ruth 4:13). Mary's question is how the child can be given when that knowing is not there.

**C2.** [L1] "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Luke 1:35
[L2] dio (G1352) means for which cause, therefore. gennao (G1080) in "born" is followed by ek sou, out of thee. eperchomai (G1904) means to come upon.
[L3] "I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father." 1 Chronicles 28:6
[L4] The angel's answer to "How shall this be" begins with the Holy Ghost coming upon her and gives "therefore" as the cause of the sonship. For Solomon the ground of sonship is election: "I have chosen him". For Jesus the ground is the conception: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God". The defender cites Acts 1:8 to make "come upon" mean power for witness. In Acts 1:8 the word stands in a promise to disciples about witnessing. In Luke 1:35 the word stands in the answer to a question about conceiving, and the result is "born of thee". Context fixes the meaning.

**C3.** The defender cites Psalm 2:7 and Acts 13:33. [L1] "And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:" Romans 1:4
[L2] horizo (G3724) means to mark out, declare.
[L4] The resurrection declares the sonship (Romans 1:4). It does not replace the cause given at conception in Luke 1:35. The two rows are consistent.

---

## D. The virgin sign

**D1.** [L1] "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." Isaiah 7:14
[L2] 'almah (H5959) is the word behind the KJV's "virgin". harah (H2029) means to conceive.
[L3] "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." Matthew 1:22-23
[L4] Matthew 1:22 ties "all this", meaning Matthew 1:18-21, to the virgin sign. The Greek behind "virgin" in Matthew 1:23 is parthenos (G3933). Luke 1:27 uses the same word twice of Mary. If Joseph begat the child, the sign cited in Matthew 1:22-23 is not fulfilled. The defender's chain leaves out Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23 entirely.

---

## E. The genealogy turns at Matthew 1:16

**E1.** [L1] "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." Matthew 1:16
[L2] gennao (G1080): the verses before use the active, "begat". In verse 16 the verb for Jesus is passive, egennethe, "was born", with ek hes, "of whom", in the feminine singular. A feminine relative cannot refer to Joseph, who is masculine, so it refers to Mary.
[L3] "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Matthew 1:2
[L4] The genealogy runs "begat, begat" through the line, then Joseph is called "the husband of Mary", and Jesus is "born" of her. That change of verb and construction is the answer to D3's naming of Joseph as father.

---

## F. Answer to D3: the "four mouths"

**F1.** [L1] "Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:48. The next verse is "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 2:49
[L2] pater (G3962) means father literally or figuratively, near or more remote, as the defender's own gloss admits.
[L3] "The Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." Luke 1:32
[L4] The same angel who speaks to Mary calls David "his father" (Luke 1:32), so pater can name an ancestor or a figurative father. Luke 2:48 uses "thy father" for Joseph. Jesus answers at once with "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49), which names another Father in the same exchange.

**F2.** [L1] "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" John 6:42
[L3] "For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me." John 6:38. Also "Is not this Joseph's son?" Luke 4:22.
[L2] nomizo (G3543) means to deem, suppose, think.
[L4] The town's "whose father and mother we know" is the crowd's belief, which John 6:42 sets against Jesus' own claim of John 6:38. Luke 3:23 supplies the correction: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". The supposing is the town's, and the text calls it supposing.

---

## G. Answer to D1, D2 and D5: the seed of David

**G1.** [L1] "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." 2 Samuel 7:12
[L2] zera (H2233) means seed, offspring.
[L3] "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed." Genesis 3:15
[L4] zera is said of the woman: "her seed" (Genesis 3:15). The word does not require a man's body as source. Every row on D1 and D2 (2 Samuel 7:12, Psalm 132:11, Acts 2:30, Romans 1:3) names David's bowels, body or loins. D5 adds the step from David's body to Joseph's body, and Luke 1:35 gives the conception's cause as the Holy Ghost coming upon Mary.

**G2.** [L1] "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Romans 1:3
[L2] ginomai (G1096) means made, become, not gennao. sperma (G4690) is offspring in a line, as in Hebrews 2:16.
[L3] "For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham." Hebrews 2:16. Also "a body hast thou prepared me" (Hebrews 10:5).
[L2] epilambanomai (G1949) in Hebrews 2:16 means to take hold of, take on. katartizo (G2675) in Hebrews 10:5 means to fit, frame, prepare.
[L4] The flesh of David's seed is real: the child is "born of thee" (Luke 1:35), of Mary. The wording is "made of the seed", "took on him the seed", and "a body hast thou prepared me". It is the language of a body provided, not of Joseph's begetting. The defender's own L2 on sperma ("including the male sperm") is a dictionary note. The verb in Romans 1:3 is ginomai.

**G3.** [L1] "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." Hebrews 7:14
[L2] anatello (G393) means to spring up, rise, as a plant or the sun. It is a different word from osphys (G3751), the loin word of Hebrews 7:10.
[L3] "Because he was of the house and lineage of David." Luke 2:4
[L4] The springing out of Juda is a statement of tribal descent. Joseph carries the house and lineage (Luke 2:4). Joseph took Mary (Matthew 1:24), named the child (Matthew 1:25), and was addressed as "thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). That is how the child is reckoned into David's house, as husband and legal father.

[L1] The registry verse says Joseph went up "to be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child" (Luke 2:5), so the one registered beside the man is his wife, already with child by the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:18). [L3] Luke 3:23 states the reckoning in its own words: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". Matthew 1:16 states the line's last link in its own words: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". [L2] nomizo (G3543) means to deem, suppose, as in Luke 3:23. [L4] Numbers 1:2 reckons "by the house of their fathers", a registry word. Luke 2:5 places the wife and the child in that registry beside Joseph, and Luke 3:23 calls the resulting sonship a supposal. The registry therefore carries Jesus into David's house by Joseph's marriage and naming, and the verses that speak of conception, Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, give the begetting to the Holy Ghost.

---

## Summary chain

1. [L1] Matthew 1:18 with [L2] sunerchomai and [L3] Luke 2:5 gives the child before the coming together, "of the Holy Ghost".
2. [L1] Matthew 1:20 with [L2] gar and gennao and [L3] Matthew 1:19 gives the reason to Joseph: the begotten child is "of the Holy Ghost".
3. [L1] Luke 1:34-35 with [L2] dio and [L3] Luke 1:27 gives Mary's question and the angel's answer: the Holy Ghost comes upon her, "therefore" the child is born of her.

6. [L1] Luke 3:23 with [L2] nomizo and [L3] Luke 2:49 and John 6:38 gives "as was supposed" against the town's "father" and Jesus' own "my Father's business".

[L4] The text gives Jesus no biological father among men. His origin is the Holy Ghost, his flesh is Mary's, and Joseph is the husband who takes Mary, names the child, and carries David's house. D5 does not stand.
